value.text:
Outbound delivery executes in the `Post` function within `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

`PostAsync` merely queues jobs; workers call `Post`, which performs the actual HTTP POST via `safeClient.Do(req)`. Internal address protection comes from three layers: `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go` blocks DNS rebinding at dial time; `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` in `validate.go` reject reserved IPs; and `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` prevents internal addresses from being configured.

The exact answer pairs `Post` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and `safeDialContext` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

The answer should pair `Post` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and `ValidateURL` with `internal/webhook/validate.go`.

The dial-time check is the true delivery-time protection, not the configuration-time validator. The final answer pairs `Post` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and `safeDialContext` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

The final answer pairs `Post` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and `isReservedIP` with `internal/webhook/validate.go`.

The final answer pairs `Post` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go` and `safeDialContext` with `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` in `validate.go` provide the underlying IP check.

h02.
Post — internal/webhook/webhook.go; safeDialContext / isReservedIP — internal/webhook/webhook.go and internal/webhook/validate.go

Outbound HTTP delivery runs in `Post`, which issues the request through `safeClient`. `PostAsync` only enqueues work; workers call `Post`. SSRF protection is `safeDialContext` on that client: it resolves the host at dial time and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, IPv6 ULA). `ValidateURL` applies the same check when a webhook URL is configured.
